01 / AGENTIC AIHACKATHON · 2026

Better decisions
start with better evidence.

Reasoning AI Agent

Outdoor work planning depends on changing conditions. I built Python pipelines that bring Malaysian weather and air quality data into a four-agent system, with evidence that can be traced and recommendations that get a second look.

  • District-level data views in Zetaris
  • Versioned evidence and persistent memory
  • Independent critic review of recommendations
PythonMulti-agent systemsSQLZetaris
Inside the build +

Developed for Open Agent Hackathon 2026. The ingestion layer brings together weather forecasts and PM2.5/PM10 observations, exposing district-level SQL views for haze analysis.

The four-agent architecture combines versioned evidence, persistent memory, and independent critic review to support outdoor work planning. My focus is on keeping the reasoning connected to its supporting data.

02 / COMPUTER VISIONPYTHON PIPELINE

From moving frames
to structured signals.

Staff Badge Detection & Tracking

A modular video pipeline that detects staff badges, tracks people across frames, and associates each badge with a person using overlap and confidence thresholds.

  • Object detection with Roboflow and OpenCV
  • Consistent person tracking with ByteTrack
  • Annotated video and frame-level CSV / JSON
OpenCVRoboflowByteTrackPython
Explore source code ↗
Inside the build +

The pipeline separates detection, tracking, badge-to-person association, and output. Bounding-box overlap and confidence thresholds connect badge detections to tracked people.

Annotated video supports visual inspection, while frame-level CSV and JSON make the detections available for further analysis.

My BSc in Astrophysics at the University of Manchester trained me to work with complex systems, interpret data, and question assumptions. I bring that same mindset to AI: understand the evidence, make the reasoning explicit, and check what the system produces.
